lidar.source: USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM, project CA_AZ_FEMA_R9_Lidar_2017_D18 (flown 2017-18, published 2021), tile USGS_1M_10_x59y405_CA_AZ_FEMA_R9_Lidar_2017_D18.tif (public domain), from prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com. Not in the repo (229 MB): python3 tests/tools/lidar.py fetch --pin 36.563057,-121.936526 --download
lidar.located_by: a map pin from the project owner on the green (36.563057, -121.936526), placed at the game pin (-22, 375.4)

frame.why: the tee is the pad at the south-west tip of the point beside the 7th green (36.56134, -121.94028; 10.0 m), 386.2 m from the pin at 59.9 degrees (422 yd; the card's 428). The game's tee -> pin is 376 yd with the pin 22 yd right, so +z is 3.4 degrees left of that line and yd_per_m = 376 / 386.2. The drive climbs the point to 21.3 m, the plateau ends in a cliff 248 m out, the green is 18.8 m up on the far side of the cove

water.why: the coast is cliffs 10-20 m high; the game's `cliff` profile drops at its shoreline, so the shoreline is read at about 7 m (6 m above the 1.15 m water), on the cliff face, not at its foot: at the water's own level the green's front-right bank (17 m down to the sea over 16 m) read as 10-12 yd of dry land
